title: Sharp maps: pullback criterion and cartesian-square calculus
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and the Kan--Quillen weak equivalences and functorial model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A commutative square is homotopy cartesian if its upper-left corner maps by a weak equivalence to the homotopy pullback of its other corners, computed by fibrant replacement. Call $p:E\to B$ sharp if every strict pullback of $p$ along every small map $T\to B$ is homotopy cartesian.
Then $p$ is sharp if and only if, for every weak equivalence $u:A\to A'$ over $B$, the map $E\times_B A\to E\times_B A'$ is a weak equivalence. Sharp maps are stable under arbitrary base change. In particular $p\times\mathrm{id}_K:E\times K\to B\times K$ is sharp for every simplicial set $K$.
For a commutative square $E'\to E$ over $B'\to B$ with $p:E\to B$ sharp, that square is homotopy cartesian if and only if its canonical map $E'\to B'\times_B E$ is a weak equivalence. If $p':E'\to B'$ is also sharp and this square is homotopy cartesian, then for every $T\to B'$ the induced comparison $E'\times_{B'}T\to E\times_B T$ is a weak equivalence; equivalently, the induced square $E'\times_{B'}T\to E$ over $T\to B$ is homotopy cartesian. Consequently two horizontally adjacent homotopy-cartesian squares whose three vertical maps are sharp have homotopy-cartesian outer rectangle. Taking the product of such a square with any simplicial set $K$ preserves homotopy-cartesianness. In particular the square $E\times K\to E\times L$ over $B\times K\to B\times L$ is homotopy cartesian for any map $K\to L$ and any sharp $p$.
